question: BCG vaccine is administered by the intradermal route into the skin over the left deltoid muscle, and a correctly placed injection produces a pale raised bleb of 5–7 mm that disappears within 30 minutes.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. BCG site: left deltoid, route: intradermal. The bleb is the quality-control marker — 5–7 mm, pale, raised, disappears within 30 minutes. No bleb = subcutaneous injection = programme error.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. BCG is given intradermally (ID) at the left deltoid. A 5–7 mm pale bleb confirms true intradermal placement. Absence of the bleb indicates subcutaneous injection and is a programme error requiring documentation.
